You do not need nineteen. You need your floor, your market and their value. Everything on this slide is a way of writing those three down.
THE 3 PARTS OF AGENCY PRICING
This method ensures you will always make a profit, even if you are charging the bare minimum.
THE FOUNDATION
Cost +
What it costs you to deliver the work plus the margin you want to run your business.
Tells you the absolute floor of what it costs to deliver your service.
Never the number you charge. It has nothing to do with what the work is worth.
The MIDDLE
Market rates
The going rate in your niche. Secret shop it, ask peers, trial and error + time on task.
Tells you the range a prospect is comfortable with.
Never should dictate your final pricing, this can become a "race to the bottom" that will destroy margins.
The Ceiling
Value based
What the value of bringing them new business is worth x the amount of market share available to them.
Tells you what your work is actually worth and how much pricing elasticity you have.
Needs their numbers and an understanding of the market data (search volume, etc).
PICK HOW TO SELL IT
Four ways to structure the same number. The difference between them is who carries the risk, and that is what you are paid for.

Margin rises as you move down. So does how much of their business you have to be able to see. Never price on a number you cannot audit yourself.
Most agencies live in scope. The money is one row down.
The Model
Build Your Price In Three Numbers
1
Your cost, and the margin you need
What does the labour to deliver this actually cost you per month, loaded? What margin does the business need to survive a bad quarter? That product is your floor. You never quote below it and you never show it to a client.
Sets the floor
2
What your niche already pays
Contractors, dentists and law firms pay different numbers for the same work. Secret shop your competitors, ask peers in the vertical, and watch what gets signed. Specialise and this number stops being a guess.
Sets the band
3
What one new client is worth to them
Ask it on the discovery call. Multiply by how many you can realistically deliver, and check the demand is there with search volume before you promise it. That is the ceiling, and your price is a fraction of it.
Sets the ceiling
Floor from your costs. Band from your niche. Ceiling from their economics. Your price lives in the gap between the band and the ceiling.
